context.body: The passage names high priesthood but not Melchizedek. The named order enters in the following chapter’s appointment argument.
context.label: The title before the Melchizedek quotation

observations.body: Jesus the Son of God is called a great high priest who passed through the heavens and was tested without sin.
observations.label: Priesthood is tied to sympathy and access

observations.body: Because of this high priest, readers are told to hold confession and approach the throne of grace for mercy and timely help.
observations.label: Confession leads to approach

payload.posture: Inspect Hebrews 4:14–16 as a bounded source before following its claims into another passage.
payload.tension: The passage connects testing, sympathy, confidence, mercy, and help without explaining the mechanism by which the priest’s experience enables access.
payload.title: Readers are called to approach through a great high priest
